verdicts.evidence: The logbook runs no experiments on real kidney transplant data (UNOS/OPTN is private and no code was released). The simulation study only tests τ=0.5 (single quantile, not multi-quantile) on synthetic data using a linear B-spline estimator instead of the FunCQNet neural network, so it does not address the claim of precise multi-quantile predictions for kidney transplant survival.

The simulation on synthetic data shows that an interaction-aware estimator reduces coefficient-function RMSE by 58–85% versus a Z-agnostic model when the true effect is Z-modulated (Table in Claim 1 page), which is a structural proxy for detecting interaction patterns. However, it uses generic covariates (Z₁~U(1,2), Z₂,Z₃~Bernoulli) rather than age and donor type, a linear estimator rather than FunCQNet, and synthetic rather than real transplant data, so it is a reduced stand-in for the clinical claim.

overall: The logbook faithfully reproduces the paper's simulation study showing that interaction-aware models recover Z-modulated coefficient functions, but it does not run any experiments on real kidney transplant data because the UNOS/OPTN registry is access-controlled and no code was released. Neither real-data claim about multi-quantile prediction precision or clinically significant age–donor-type interactions is directly tested.
